newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council chief summons Israeli on housing plan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council chief summons Israeli on housing plan.

text.p: Security Council President Francesco Paolo Fulci of Italy said on Tuesday he would call in Israeli charge d'affaires David Peleg to express concern about a plan for the construction of 132 housing units for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.
If Israel's response was not satisfactory, the council could pursue the matter, he added.

Fulci told reporters that council members, during closed-door consultations, had taken up a letter from the Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, complaining about the housing plan and calling for council action.
"Concerns on this issue were expressed unanimously by the negative influence the settlement plan can have on the peace process," Fulci said.
He said he had been asked by council members to call in the Israeli diplomat "to express the concern of the council and to report on the...outcome of this demarche.
"Because if the response by the Israeli government is not going to be satisfactory, the members of the council reserve (the right) to take up the matter again," he added.
Kidwa said in his letter last Friday that the building plan for the Ras al-Amud district of East Jerusalem violated the Fourth Geneva Convention and U.N. resolutions.
He also said Israel was violating a 1993 accord with the PLO in which they agreed to negotiate the status of Jerusalem, among other things, as part of a final settlement.
Israel captured East Jerusalem from Jordan during the 1967 Middle East war and later declared the undivided city its capital.
